summary.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 20% YoY to INR178 crores and EBITDA 24% to INR90 crores (50.7% margin), with footfalls up 22%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew 20% YoY to INR178 crores, with footfalls up 22% to over 11.5 lakh visitors and parks revenue up 22% to INR161 crores. EBITDA rose 24% to INR90 crores and PAT rose 30% to INR58 crores. Management attributed the soft spots to an extended heat wave that kept Khopoli park non-operational for about two weeks and a shift in some CBSE school holiday calendars, and said it deliberately priced softer to build footfall. Management also announced the acquisition of a 50.002% stake in Mehsana Next Parks (Shanku's Water Park) for INR50 crores and the entry into indoor entertainment via a Hello Park franchise.

segments.name: Mumbai-Pune catchment (4 parks)
segments.commentary: Revenue +18% YoY on footfalls +19%; largest contributor and most affected by heat wave and Khopoli closure.

segments.name: Rest of Maharashtra (Shirdi, Saiteerth)
segments.commentary: Revenue +33% YoY on footfalls +14%; ARPU +17% on better product mix and higher guest spend.

segments.name: Gujarat (Surat, Mehsana)
segments.commentary: Footfalls +32% but revenue only +15%; ARPU lower YoY on visitor mix change and promotional pricing at Surat.

segments.name: Hospitality (Novotel Imagicaa, 287 keys, Khopoli)
segments.commentary: Revenue largely stable despite occupancy at 62%; ARR INR9,657.

guidance_outlook: Target of 12 parks by 2030, adding roughly one park a year; 12 count includes smaller outdoor parks but excludes Hello Park indoor centres.
Hello Park: plan to add 2-3 indoor centres a year; first centre in Hyderabad (Lake Shore Y Junction Mall) later this year; second at Phoenix Mall, Surat.
Pricing: management said headroom exists to lift ticket prices; a price action plan is expected from Q3-Q4 FY27.
Mehsana Next Parks becomes a subsidiary now; consolidation reflected from Q2 FY27 onward. Management fee of 6-10% of revenue expected.
Debt/EBITDA: average 2.5-3.0x, peak up to 3.0-3.5x for limited periods.
Dave & Buster's integration into the listed company: not expected in the next three to four months; no firm timeline.
capex_capacity: New park cost guided at INR200-450 crores depending on location and size; B-tier city park about INR150 crores on 20-25 acres; A-category metro park about INR450 crores with about 25 rides.
Maintenance capex expensed in P&L at about 6-8% of revenue; new attractions capex budgeted at about 5% of top line.
Hello Park capex INR8-12 crores per centre (about 10,000 sq ft in malls); EBITDA margin 24-25% after mall rentals; payback 3-4 years; royalty 5% of revenue.
Ferris wheel of about 45 m costs INR20-25 crores landed in India.
Sabarmati Riverfront (Ahmedabad) project expected to be partly operational in the coming year if all goes well.
Funding: mix of internal accruals and moderate debt; banking limits approved by a couple of leading banks.
demand_pricing: Heat wave led to around two weeks of non-operation at Khopoli; some CBSE schools shifted holiday patterns; hotel bookings tapered during heat wave.
Management consciously ran softer ticket pricing this quarter to drive footfall and non-ticket spend; no price hikes taken yet during integration.
Surat ARPU fell as management tested price elasticity; revenue still above FY25 levels per management.
Ticketing and F&B/retail revenue reported combined by catchment; management agreed to split them in future press notes.
Spiritual parks: management in talks with state governments to replicate the Shirdi model; one or two locations expected in two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: Is like-for-like growth weak given Q1 FY25 revenue of about INR184 crores vs INR177 crores now, and is ARPU flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed the heat wave, Khopoli closure and school calendar shifts; it chose softer pricing to push footfall and expects headroom to correct pricing over the next three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Hello Park economics: margins after rent, royalty and year-one footfall/ARPU?
qa_highlights.answer: Ticket price target INR800-900; ticketing about 65-70% of revenue; EBITDA margin 24-25% after mall rent; royalty 5% of revenue; capex about INR10 crores per 10,000 sq ft centre; payback 3-4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Will promoters convert warrants priced at INR73.5?
qa_highlights.answer: Jai Malpani said the promoter group is positive and the conversion will happen before the due date.

qa_highlights.question: Funding for large capex and debt levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Mix of internal accruals and moderate debt; average debt/EBITDA 2.5-3x, up to 3-3.5x for a limited period.

qa_highlights.question: Dave & Buster's integration timing?
qa_highlights.answer: No firm timeline; the model is still being stabilised; not expected in the next three to four months.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Gujarat ARPU drop sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Surat price sensitivity; a deliberate price test; adjoining hotel and mall not yet operational; expected to recover over time.

risks_watch: Weather and seasonality: Q1 is the strongest quarter and Q2-Q3 are weak; the heat wave and monsoon drove the Q1 shortfall.
Pricing: ARPU has been flat for some time and the Gujarat ARPU fell sharply; the price-hike plan is due from Q3-Q4 FY27.
Gujarat concentration (Surat, Mehsana, Ahmedabad) as flagged by analysts.
Debt and capex funding for INR200-450 crore parks; the 2.5-3x debt/EBITDA guideline.
Promoter warrant conversion at INR73.5, timing still to be seen.
Hello Park execution: first centre in Hyderabad later this year; royalty of 5% and mall-dependent economics.
Disclosure: management moved to half-yearly calls; ticketing vs F&B split to be disclosed from next results.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, margins and the expansion pipeline, but defensive on like-for-like growth and ARPU, which it attributed to weather and a deliberate price test. Evasive on Dave & Buster's timing and on the cost of new parks.
